beats.beat: The company sells four product groups: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM). These are specialty chemicals used across multiple industries.

It does not sell directly to end-users. Instead, it has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell products through the promoter's network. This makes the company heavily dependent on the promoter for revenue generation.
Customer concentration is high: the top 10 customers accounted for around 59% of revenue from operations in each of FY2015, FY2016, and FY2017.
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka, with cumulative exports of ₹1,068.18 lakh over the past five years.

business.purpose: Explain the product categories, business model (reliance on promoter's distribution network), customer concentration, and export markets.

beats.beat: Profit after tax turned positive from FY2015 onwards after two loss-making years. PAT was ₹(27.40) lakh in FY2013, ₹(12.17) lakh in FY2014, then ₹149.58 lakh in FY2015, ₹90.18 lakh in FY2016, ₹174.82 lakh in FY2017, and ₹132.75 lakh for the six months ended September 2017.

Cash flow from operations has been volatile. It was ₹200.97 lakh in FY2013, ₹127.73 lakh in FY2014, ₹422.36 lakh in FY2015, ₹802.59 lakh in FY2016, but turned negative at ₹(349.75) lakh in FY2017, before recovering to ₹124.86 lakh in the six months ended September 2017.

Basic earnings per share (EPS) moved from losses to profits: ₹(0.45) in FY2013, ₹(0.20) in FY2014, ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.43 in FY2017, and ₹1.48 for the six months ended September 2017.

beats.beat: The promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited. They collectively hold 89,48,270 equity shares, amounting to 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity share capital.
The promoter group (excluding promoters) holds only 21,510 shares, or 0.24% of pre-issue share capital. Post-IPO, promoter holding will dilute but remain dominant.
The company has entered into related-party transactions in the past five years and may continue to do so. Details are referenced in the financial statements (page 223 of the DRHP).

There have been instances of non-filing or delayed filing of statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies, and the company has not yet obtained certain statutory licenses for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals segment (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at ₹1,000 billion in FY2017, growing at a 10-12% CAGR between FY2014 and FY2017.
CRISIL Research forecasts specialty chemicals to grow at 12-14% CAGR going forward, with sub-segments like construction chemicals and water chemicals expected to grow at 15% CAGR.
The industry is highly fragmented: small and medium enterprises hold 70-75% of the market share. Only a few Indian players can compete with global giants on product development and innovation.

Key demand drivers include rising consumption, end-use demand from a growing middle class, government initiatives (Draft National Chemical Policy, 100% FDI), and global factors such as China's stricter environmental regulations reducing its specialty chemicals output.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals — Functional Additives, Chemically Modified Minerals, Soft Minerals, and Hard Minerals — with its products marketed largely through the network of its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited.
The company is raising money through an IPO on the NSE EMERGE (SME) platform, with proceeds earmarked for a new manufacturing plant and general corporate purposes.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who 20 Microns Nano Minerals is, what it does, and that it is raising capital via an SME IPO.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares (the DRHP does not disclose the number of shares or the split between fresh issue and offer for sale). The objects of the issue include funding capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and general corporate purposes.
A secondary objective is to create a public trading market for the equity shares on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE) and enhance the company's visibility and brand.
The lead manager to the issue is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited; the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

beats.beat: No long-term agreements with customers or suppliers. The company relies on purchase orders, meaning volume and pricing can change abruptly, jeopardising revenue stability.
Negative cash flows in recent years. Operating cash flow was negative ₹349.75 lakh in FY2017. Sustained negative cash flow could force the company to seek additional debt or equity.
Contingent liabilities of ₹29.11 lakh as on September 30, 2017. If these materialise, they could erode profitability.

Non-compliance with statutory licenses for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia. The company has not yet obtained required licenses and could face penalties or operational disruptions.

High promoter concentration (99.76% pre-issue) and a history of related-party transactions. The company's dependence on its corporate promoter for sales and the presence of related-party deals create potential conflicts of interest.
